records.label: Patient 1
quotes: Patient 1 showed macrocephaly, behavioral difficulty, and learning disability with a hemizygous SMARCA1 variant (NM_003069.5:c.1795 C > T p.[Gln599*]) leading to nonsense-mediated decay.
Both variants were inherited from their unaffected healthy mothers.

records.label: Patient 2
quotes: Patient 2 had ataxia and speech delay with a hemizygous missense variant (NM_003069.5:c.1343 G > T p.[Arg448Leu]).
Both variants were inherited from their unaffected healthy mothers.

notes.statement: Nishimura et al. (2025) used exome sequencing to identify novel hemizygous SMARCA1 variants in 2 unrelated males with X-linked intellectual disability: a nonsense variant (Q599X) leading to nonsense-mediated decay and a missense variant (R448L). Both variants were inherited from unaffected mothers.
quotes: Here, we report two unrelated male patients with XLID due to novel SMARCA1 variants detected by exome sequencing.
Both variants were inherited from their unaffected healthy mothers.

notes.statement: Structural modeling by Nishimura et al. (2025) suggested that the R448L missense variant might destabilize interactions between SMARCA1 and nucleosomal DNA, contributing to an aberrant effect of the mutant protein.
quotes: Structural modeling suggested that the missense variant, p.(Arg448Leu) might destabilize interactions between SMARCA1 and nucleosomal DNA, thereby contributing to the abberant effect of mutant SMARCA1 protein.

notes.statement: Riazuddin et al. (2017) performed exome sequencing in 121 consanguineous Pakistani families with recessive intellectual disability. In 30 families they identified homozygous or compound heterozygous variants in single novel candidate genes, including TMEM222. None of these variants was found in 213 ethnically matched controls.
quotes: In 60 families, we identified homozygous or compound heterozygous DNA variants in a single gene, 30 affecting reported ID genes and 30 affecting novel candidate ID genes.
None of the variants were found in 213 unrelated, ethnically matched control individuals, indicating that they are not indigenous Pakistani polymorphisms.

notes.statement: Riazuddin et al. (2017) found that all of the new candidate recessive ID genes were expressed in the human brain from early development to adulthood. The genes were significantly co-expressed in the frontal cortex from 12 postconception weeks onward and in the temporal-parietal and subcortical regions from infancy through late childhood.
quotes: All new candidate ARID genes are expressed in the human brain from a very early development stage to adulthood (Supplementary Table S8).
the ID genes are significantly co-expressed in the frontal cortex region from 12 p.c.w. onwards, and in the temporal–parietal and sub-cortical regions from infancy to late childhood

notes.statement: Lopes et al. (2016) used array CGH and whole-exome sequencing in 19 Portuguese patients with Rett syndrome-like phenotypes. In 6 patients they found variants in genes already linked to neurodevelopmental disorders, including a de novo variant in ZNF238. They concluded that these findings broaden the phenotypic spectrum of known neurodevelopmental disorder genes to include Rett-like presentations.
quotes: Variants in genes previously implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders (NDD) were identified in six patients (32%): de novo variants in EEF1A2, STXBP1 and ZNF238 were found in three patients
These findings expand the phenotypical spectrum of previously known NDD genes to encompass RTT-like clinical presentations

notes.statement: In a whole-exome sequencing study of 128 mostly consanguineous families with neurogenetic disorders that often included brain malformations, Karaca et al. (2015) identified HELZ as one of two potential candidate genes that encode RNA helicases, the other being DHX37. The text does not give clinical or variant details for the HELZ family.
quotes: We identified two potential candidate genes which function as RNA helicases: DHX37 and HELZ.
We applied whole exome sequencing to 128 mostly consanguineous families with neurogenetic disorders that often included brain malformations.
